- When sentiment is consistently negative (last 3–5 days), model tends to over-forecast; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 5–7 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent peak for next 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment shows strong positive momentum (e.g., +0.2+ for 3+ days), model under-forecasts; add 1–2% to forecast for next 5–7 days.  
- Model tends to over-forecast in early horizon (1–3 days) when sentiment is neutral or slightly negative; apply 1–3% downward adjustment for first 3 days.  
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.  
- Sentiment reversal (e.g., from +0.2 to -0.1) triggers model lag; adjust forecast to align with 3–5 day sentiment shift, not 10–15 day lag.
